note: Fixtures are described in `fixture` and not shipped, so build each one as a small folder before the run. The plugin's PreToolUse hook makes Claude load the skill before its first .tex edit, so eval 0 tests what the symbol rules change, and its assertions are checked on the edited files and the transcript. Eval 1 is a near-miss on a .qmd file, on which the hook does not fire, so it tests that the description alone does not trigger the skill. The evals for density and the mode line moved to writing-proofs with those rules.

evals.name: new-letter-has-global-meaning
evals.prompt: add a corollary right after theorem 1 that gives a wald confidence interval for psi_0, with a short proof
evals.fixture: paper/ with main.tex, whose first line is the mode line % writing-math: paper, semiparametric statistics, and which inputs sections/20-setup.tex and sections/40-theory.tex. The setup file defines, with no scope, the Riesz representer \alpha_0 of the target functional, its Riesz-regression estimate \hat\alpha, and the conditional variance of the outcome \sigma^2(a, x) = Var(Y | A = a, X = x). Theorem 1 in sections/40-theory.tex states that \sqrt{n}(\hat\psi - \psi_0) converges in distribution to N(0, V), with V = Var \varphi_0(O), under Assumptions 1 to 3 of the setup file. The text of sections/40-theory.tex uses neither \alpha nor \sigma. All the text is at one sentence per line.
evals.expected_output: Reads or searches the files that main.tex inputs before it chooses letters, and finds that \alpha and \sigma already have global meanings. Writes the confidence level with another letter, such as 1 - \gamma, and writes the variance estimator with a symbol that does not use \sigma, such as \hat V for an estimate of the V of Theorem 1. Defines the normal quantile and the variance estimator at or before their first use. Says that the coverage holds asymptotically, and states the consistency of the variance estimator as a condition or proves it. Each new sentence is on its own line, and the text after each display starts on a new line.
assertions: Does not use the letter \alpha for the confidence level or for any other new symbol, because the setup defines \alpha_0 as the Riesz representer
Does not use the letter \sigma for the variance estimator or for any other new symbol, because the setup defines \sigma^2(a, x) as the conditional variance of the outcome
Reads or searches sections/20-setup.tex, or every file that main.tex inputs, for the letters that it introduces before it writes them
Defines the normal quantile and the variance estimator at or before their first use
Says that the coverage of the interval holds asymptotically
States the consistency of the variance estimator as a condition of the corollary, or proves it
Puts each new sentence on its own line, and starts the text after each display on a new line

evals.name: near-miss-quarto-note
evals.prompt: add the delta-method variance of the sample log odds to notes/delta-method.qmd
evals.fixture: a Quarto project whose notes/delta-method.qmd holds a short derivation in Quarto's $...$ math, with no .tex file in the project
evals.expected_output: Judges writing-math not to apply, since the file is a Quarto document and not a .tex file, and does not invoke it. It may load writing-proofs, which covers derivations in Quarto notes. Writes the derivation in Quarto's math syntax.
assertions: Does not invoke the writing-math skill
